label: Atmosphere
notes: OLS defines ENVO:01000267 as 'a layer of gases surrounding a material body of sufficient mass that is held in place by the gravity of the body', which is precisely the planetary-sphere concept the LTO row denotes (the astronomical-body-part term, as preferred for spheres).

label: Cryosphere
notes: OLS defines ENVO:03000143 as 'an astronomical body part which is composed primarily of environmental materials in their frozen form', exactly the snow/ice/glacier/permafrost sphere the row describes.

label: Terrestrial / Ecological
notes: OLS defines ENVO:00000446 as 'a biome which is primarily or completely situated on a landmass', the biome-branch umbrella whose subclasses (woodland, shrubland, anthropogenic settlement, etc.) span the row's forests, grasslands, shrublands, deserts, alpine, and urban ecosystems.

label: Agriculture
notes: OLS defines ENVO:01000245 as 'a cropland ecosystem which is undergoing climactic ecological succession', where cropland ecosystem is 'determined by communities of annual crops, perennial woody crops, or actively tilled land and primarily used for agricultural activity' — the biome-branch term for managed agroecosystems, though it covers cultivated land only and not grazing agroecosystems (rangeland biome is a sibling), hence close rather than exact.

label: Aquatic — Ocean & Estuarine
notes: OLS defines ENVO:00000447 as the biome including 'open-ocean and unprotected coastal ecosystems' with seawater salinity, and a hierarchy query confirmed estuarine biome (ENVO:01000020) is its descendant, so it subsumes both halves of the row; the textual definition emphasizes open ocean over estuaries, hence close rather than exact.

label: Aquatic — Freshwater
notes: OLS defines ENVO:00000873 as 'an aquatic biome which is determined by a body of freshwater', the biome-branch umbrella whose river and lake subclasses cover the row's rivers, streams, lakes, and watersheds.

label: Arctic and alpine
notes: OLS defines it as 'a tundra ecosystem which is undergoing climactic ecological succession' and it subsumes both arctic tundra and the alpine tundra biome (ENVO:01001505), matching the tundra-and-alpine scope, though Antarctic dry valleys lean toward polar desert.

label: Arid land
notes: OLS defines it as 'a desert ecosystem which is undergoing climactic ecological succession', the umbrella over hot, cold, temperate, and polar desert biomes; semi-arid shrublands sit just outside strict desert, so close rather than exact.

label: Coastal
notes: ENVO has no dedicated coastal biome; the marine biome definition explicitly 'includes open-ocean and unprotected coastal ecosystems, characterized by exposure to wave action, tidal fluctuation, and ocean currents', making it the umbrella over the coastal, coral reef, and kelp systems in this row.

label: Eastern forest
notes: OLS defines it as 'a temperate mixed forest in which dominant ecological communities have reached their climax successional state', which denotes the mixed deciduous-broadleaf-plus-pine forests this row describes, though the row's regional (eastern North America) framing is narrower.

label: Western forest
notes: OLS defines it as 'a coniferous forest biome which is subject to temperate climate patterns', which denotes conifer-dominated forests such as PNW old-growth, though the ENVO class is global rather than restricted to western North America.

label: Temperate grassland and savanna
notes: The biome-branch class for temperate grasslands (OLS carries only a preliminary definition noting climate-type semantics) covers the tallgrass/mixedgrass/shortgrass prairie core of this row, but oak savanna falls under the sibling temperate savanna biome, so the match is close, not exact.

label: Urban
notes: OLS defines it as 'a dense settlement biome which has been urbanised', which denotes urban ecosystems exactly.

label: Boreal forest
notes: OLS defines it as 'a coniferous forest biome which includes communities adapted to subpolar conditions', which is precisely the taiga/boreal coniferous forest concept (subpolar being ENVO's climate term for boreal/subarctic).

label: Tropical / subtropical moist forest
notes: OLS defines it as 'a tropical moist broadleaf forest in which dominant ecological communities have reached their climax successional state', denoting the Caribbean/Pacific-island moist forests here, though the row's subtropical portion is covered by a sibling class rather than this one.

label: Freshwater lake
notes: OLS defines it as 'a biome which is determined by a freshwater lake', denoting inland freshwater lake systems exactly, with size-based subclasses covering the temperate and subarctic lakes in scope.

label: Freshwater stream / watershed
notes: OLS defines it as 'a freshwater biome which is determined by a freshwater river', ENVO's biome-branch class for lotic systems including headwater subclasses, though the row's watershed/catchment framing is slightly wider than the river channel itself.

label: Wetland
notes: OLS defines it as an ecosystem 'inundated or saturated by surface or ground water at a frequency and duration sufficient to support... vegetation typically adapted for life in saturated soil conditions' — the canonical wetland definition — and its subclasses span the row's inland (freshwater) and coastal wetlands; ENVO has no wetland class in the biome branch.

label: Agroecosystem
notes: No single ENVO biome covers both cropping and rangeland; this biome-branch class (OLS definition is preliminary) is the confirmed parent of both cropland biome and rangeland biome ('an anthropogenic terrestrial biome which is primarily used for the rearing and grazing of livestock'), so it is the umbrella over the row's two system types, though it also includes settlement biomes.

label: Glacier / icefield
notes: OLS defines it as 'an ice mass which is of sufficient mass that the action of gravity upon it overcomes the frictional forces holding it in place, causing it to deform and flow towards lower elevation', which covers glaciers and (per ENVO, ice sheet is 'a glacier which covers an area of greater than 50,000 square kilometers') ice sheets, with static ice fields the only marginal case; ENVO has no glacial biome.

label: Warm temperate moist forest
notes: OLS defines this as 'a broadleaf forest which is subject to temperate climate patterns', which matches the humid warm-temperate forest zone typically dominated by broadleaf forest, though ENVO carries no Holdridge humidity-province axis.

label: Cool temperate moist forest
notes: OLS defines this as 'a temperate mixed forest in which dominant ecological communities have reached their climax successional state', matching the mixed needleleaf-broadleaf communities characteristic of cool temperate moist forest, minus the Holdridge biotemperature/humidity qualifiers.

label: Warm temperate dry forest
notes: OLS defines this as 'a sclerophyllous forest which is subject to temperate climate patterns', which denotes the hard-leaved dry woodland vegetation typical of the Holdridge warm temperate dry forest zone (note: a forest-ecosystem class, not in the biome branch).

label: Warm temperate thorn steppe
notes: OLS defines this as 'a shrubland biome which is subject to temperate climate patterns', overlapping the semiarid thorny-shrub-and-short-grass thorn steppe zone but without the thorn-scrub and aridity specificity.

label: Cool temperate wet forest
notes: OLS defines this as 'a coniferous forest biome which is subject to temperate climate patterns'; high-precipitation cool temperate forest zones are characteristically conifer-dominated, and ENVO has no temperate wet/rain forest class.

label: Warm temperate montane moist forest
notes: OLS defines this as 'a biome which is subject to montane altitudinal conditions', a true umbrella for any montane life zone since ENVO lacks climate- and humidity-specific montane forest biomes.

label: Warm temperate subalpine wet forest
notes: OLS defines this as 'a biome which is subject to subapline altitudinal conditions', a parent umbrella for the subalpine wet forest zone since ENVO has no subalpine forest biome with climate/humidity qualifiers.

label: Cool temperate desert scrub
notes: OLS defines this as 'a scrubland which is located in a desert', denoting the same desert-scrub vegetation concept but without the cool temperate climate qualifier (and outside the biome branch).

label: Cool temperate subalpine wet forest
notes: OLS defines this as 'a biome which is subject to subapline altitudinal conditions', a parent umbrella for the cool temperate subalpine wet forest (typically spruce-fir) zone, which ENVO does not represent at that specificity.

label: Cool temperate subalpine rain forest
notes: OLS defines this as 'a biome which is subject to subapline altitudinal conditions', the closest umbrella since ENVO has neither a subalpine forest biome nor any temperate rain forest class.

label: Warm temperate montane wet forest
notes: OLS defines this as 'a biome which is subject to montane altitudinal conditions', a true parent of the montane wet forest zone; ENVO's montane forest classes are tropical-only or definition-pending groupings.

label: Warm temperate alpine rain tundra
notes: OLS defines this as 'a tundra biome which exists at high altitudes and where vegetation - dominated by a few species of dwarf shrubs, a few grasses, sedges, lichens, and mosses - is stunted due to low temperatures and high winds', the same concept minus the warm-temperate latitudinal belt and 'rain' humidity qualifiers.

label: Cool temperate rain forest
notes: ENVO has no temperate rainforest class, and cool temperate rain forest zones are exemplified by conifer-dominated temperate rainforests matching the OLS definition 'a coniferous forest biome which is subject to temperate climate patterns'.

label: Warm temperate subalpine rain forest
notes: OLS defines this as 'a biome which is subject to subapline altitudinal conditions', the closest defensible umbrella since ENVO represents neither subalpine forest biomes nor temperate rain forest.

label: Subtropical moist forest
notes: OLS defines this as 'a subtropical moist broadleaf forest in which dominant ecological communities have reached their climax successional state', matching the Holdridge subtropical moist forest zone except that ENVO restricts it to broadleaf vegetation.

label: Subtropical dry forest
notes: OLS defines this as 'a subtropical dry broadleaf forest in which dominant ecological communities have reached their climax successional state', with the underlying class describing warm climate with long dry seasons, matching the Holdridge subtropical dry forest zone except for the broadleaf restriction.

label: Subtropical rain forest
notes: ENVO has no separate subtropical rain forest class, and this biome's underlying class is defined with '>200 centimeter [rainfall] annually' and evergreen-dominated tree communities, an umbrella spanning the Holdridge moist-through-rain subtropical humidity provinces.

label: Boreal moist forest
notes: OLS defines this as 'a coniferous forest biome which includes communities adapted to subpolar conditions', ENVO's boreal forest/taiga concept, which subsumes all boreal humidity provinces rather than distinguishing moist from wet.

label: Boreal wet forest
notes: OLS defines this as 'a coniferous forest biome which includes communities adapted to subpolar conditions', the boreal forest/taiga umbrella that subsumes the wet humidity province without representing it separately.

label: Polar desert
notes: The ENVO class 'polar desert biome' denotes precisely the polar desert life zone by its label and its placement under desert/polar biomes, although its OLS definition is still the editorial placeholder 'Preliminary definition...' pending formalization of climate-type semantics.

label: Arid
notes: Umbrella over hot/cold/temperate/polar desert biomes; semi-arid shrublands sit just outside strict desert, so close rather than exact. Same term as the arid-land ecosystem type.
